Subject: Procurement questionnaire: measurement & visibility for SLA commitments

Hi Ben,

Thanks for taking our call yesterday. As part of our procurement packet I need to capture how Redwood measures and exposes uptime/latency commitments. Below are the specific items our compliance team requires. Can you confirm and attach any supporting artifacts?

1) How are availability and latency SLOs instrumented? (point-in-time vs rolling window, percentile used, sample granularity)
2) Do you provide customers with read-only access to the same dashboards you use? If so, what is the entitlement process and RBAC scope?
3) What is your sampling policy for high-throughput customers (are tail latencies undersampled?)
4) How are incidents and SLA breaches communicated and evidenced (postmortems, metric extracts, time series snapshots)?
5) Is raw telemetry retained for audit (how long) and can we request extracts for audits?
6) If we need a temporary exception to an SLO (e.g., on-prem migration, bulk batch jobs), what is the exception process and typical turnaround?

If possible please attach a short packet (dashboard screenshots, runbook excerpt, retention table) and indicate who on your side we should interview for a short call to close the packet.

Appreciate a response by EOD Friday so we can keep procurement on schedule.

Best,

Hi Thomas — thanks for the clear list. I've attached a concise packet that addresses each item (Service_Metrics_Packet.pdf) and pasted short answers below. If anything needs more detail we can follow up by call; I can make time tomorrow.

Quick answers (summary):
1) Instrumentation: we measure availability as percentage of successful API responses at the inter-router boundary, calculated on a rolling 30-day window and reported as 99.95th percentile for latency measurements (p99 for request completion). Sample granularity is per-request with continuous batching metadata; metrics emitted at 1s resolution and aggregated to 1m for dashboarding.

2) Dashboard access: yes — we provide read-only dashboards in the Redwood Console. Entitlement is via a HIPAA/PCI-safe RBAC profile for customers: read-only viewer to per-customer views; onboarding is an access request from your procurement lead + customer admin SSO (SAML/OIDC). Typical lead time: 24–72 hours for standard accounts; for enterprise approvals we can expedite. Link: https://console.redwood.ai/dashboards/finserv-readonly

3) Sampling: we do not sample tail latency for API request traces used in SLO computation — every request record contributes to p99. For detailed distributed traces we apply adaptive sampling (higher for error/tail events). For very high throughput customers we can enable shard-level aggregation to preserve granularity without ingress overload.

4) Incidents & evidence: incidents are communicated via email + PagerDuty to named contacts; SLA breaches trigger an evidence packet with time series exports (CSV) and a short validated postmortem within 5 business days. We attach a runbook snapshot in the packet (runbook-snapshot.txt).

5) Retention: aggregated metrics retained for 2 years; raw per-request telemetry retained for 90 days by default. Audit extracts can be requested; for regulatory audits we support 3rd-party attestation and can extend retention under contract.

6) Exceptions: exceptions (temporary SLO carve-outs) are requested via a formal exception request form, reviewed by our Reliability & Legal teams. Typical turnaround is 3–7 business days; emergency short-term exceptions can be approved within 24 hours with post-approval mitigation.

Attachments: Service_Metrics_Packet.pdf (dashboard screenshots, SLO definitions table), runbook-snapshot.txt (example incident runbook excerpt).

We can schedule a 30-minute call with Marissa Cole (Reliability lead) and Karthik Iyer (Product) to walk through the packet and answer any technical queries — what time works for you?

Thanks,
